criteria.text: FINDINGS.md cites a line in formatMoney (billing.ts 301-305) for the missing zero-padding of cents.
FINDINGS.md explains that formatMoney does not zero-pad the cents, so amounts with fewer than 10 cents print wrongly (1005 cents shows as $10.5, not $10.05).
FINDINGS.md cites a line in the usageCharge tier loop (billing.ts 214-222).

FINDINGS.md explains that usageCharge uses a tier's cumulative upTo cap as the number of units in that tier instead of upTo minus the previous cap, so tiers after the first bill too many units at their rate.
FINDINGS.md cites the proration in changePlan (billing.ts 181-192) or prorationFactor (billing.ts 138-143).

FINDINGS.md explains that prorationFactor returns the share of the period already used while changePlan treats it as the unused share, so an upgrade credits and charges the elapsed part of the period instead of the remaining part.
FINDINGS.md cites the credit deduction in applyCredit (billing.ts 233-237), its call in buildInvoice (261), previewInvoice (274-283) or the deduction in finaliseInvoice (294).

FINDINGS.md explains that applyCredit deducts account credit inside buildInvoice, so previewInvoice changes the account despite its contract, and/or finaliseInvoice deducts the same credit a second time.
FINDINGS.md cites the tax and credit calculation in buildInvoice (billing.ts 258-260).
FINDINGS.md explains that credit is applied after tax, to the taxed amount, when the rules require credit to come off the discounted subtotal before tax so that tax is charged only on what remains.
FINDINGS.md cites planChangeTiming (billing.ts 152-156) or its use in changePlan (176-179).

FINDINGS.md explains that planChangeTiming decides by included units rather than monthly price, so a move to a cheaper plan with more units takes effect immediately with proration and a credit instead of waiting for the period end (or a pricier plan with no extra units wrongly waits).

Every finding in FINDINGS.md other than the six bugs above describes behaviour that is actually wrong; a finding that misreads the code or flags correct behaviour as a bug fails this criterion. The following are debatable design points, not false positives, in either variant: an upgrade's next invoice charging the new plan's full monthly price alongside the proration lines; usage being priced on the new plan after an upgrade; totals or subtotals that could go negative; validatePlan never being called by the invoicing path; a zero-length period dividing by zero in prorationFactor; long line descriptions overflowing the rendered invoice width; a NaN tax rate passing validateAccount.
